claims: The NASA Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026.
The NASA Artemis II mission launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The NASA Artemis II mission launched from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The Artemis II mission crew consisted of four astronauts.
The Artemis II mission was a 10-day mission.
The Artemis II mission marked the first crewed flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
The Artemis II launch occurred at 18:35 EDT.
The Artemis II launch site was Launch Complex 39B, Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
The Artemis II vehicle was the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Artemis II mission goal was a 10-day around-the-moon journey with a four-person crew.
The Artemis II launch was originally targeted for 6:24 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II launch was officially confirmed at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II launch followed a brief wait to resolve a technical issue with the crew capsule's battery
